author: DTrim99
body:
Confirmed — this is the Maryland cousin of the Maine gap in #1056, and the Comptroller memo you quoted matches the current form instructions. The [2025 Resident Booklet, Instruction 18 (Line 22)](https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/2025/resident-booklet.pdf#page=22) states the age disregard without any marriage restriction: "If you do not meet the minimum age requirement under the federal credit and are otherwise eligible for the federal credit for those without a qualifying child, you may claim the state earned income credit (calculate federal earned income credit disregarding the minimum age requirement)." Married couples — joint or separate, with or without a qualifying child — then use Worksheet 18A: Line 22 = 50% of the federal credit, and ½ × $649 = $324.50 → your $325. They can also claim the Line 44 refundable credit (Worksheet 21A: 45% of the federal credit minus Maryland tax).

On the PolicyEngine side this is a one-variable wiring gap: it already computes `federal_eitc_without_age_minimum` ($649 here), but only uses it for single/head-of-household/surviving-spouse childless filers (Worksheet 18A.1); the married-couple branch multiplies the actual federal EITC, which is $0 because both spouses are under 25. Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#8934.

One question about the record: txpydata.raw has year=2024, but $325 is ½ × the **2025** childless federal maximum ($649) — for 2024 we'd expect ½ × $632 = $316 on Line 22. Was the TaxAct return prepared for 2025? (Also, the two scanned PDFs in the out2psl/1052 directory return 403 Forbidden, if you get a chance to fix their permissions.)
